title: OneDrive and SharePoint: single hero link for file and folder sharing
summary: Hold: the briefing says Microsoft has not documented which sharing settings remove hero link scopes, but the cited PowerShell reference explicitly documents the restrictions on Anyone. The rollout, defaults and commands are supported; licensing and two navigation paths need smaller clarifications.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The new OneDrive and SharePoint sharing experience has one hero link per file or folder.
claims.quote: In OneDrive and SharePoint, each item has one **hero link**.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can change the hero link's audience without creating or redistributing a new URL.
claims.quote: A hero link allows users to share a single link for an item, then change the audience and permissions for that link without needing to create a new URL.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Users can change the hero link's permissions without creating a new URL.
claims.quote: Changing the scope or permission doesn't create a new URL.

claims.quote: Users can share an item with specific people or security groups through **Add people**. This action grants direct access to the item.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Effective access is the highest permission granted by direct access, groups, parent folder or site, the hero link or another link.
claims.quote: A user's effective access is the highest permission granted by any source: direct access, a group, the parent folder or site, the hero link, or another sharing link.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Restricting the hero link does not remove permissions from other sources; reducing effective access requires changing every source granting higher permission.
claims.quote: For example, a user with **Can edit** direct access can still edit the item when the hero link grants **Can view**. Reducing access requires changing each source that grants a higher permission.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published a license requirement specific to the hero link.
claims.quote: To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing explanation with: 'SharePoint users need an assigned license that includes SharePoint. OneDrive is included in Microsoft 365 and Office 365 plans, in SharePoint plans, or a standalone OneDrive plan. No requirement specific to the hero link is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/sharepoint-online-service-description/sharepoint-online-service-description and https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/onedrive-for-business-service-description. Retain the narrower absence of a hero-link-specific meter.

claims.where: controls[2].note
claims.claim: No complete mapping of each organization-level sharing setting to hero link scopes is given in the cited documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: '"hero link" "sharing policies" Anyone organization settings'; read shareable-links, sharing settings and Set-SPOSite. Found the Anyone tenant restriction and site fallback, but not a complete setting-by-setting mapping for every hero link scope.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].note with: 'Available hero link scopes depend on the organization's sharing policies. Anyone is available only if anonymous links are allowed at tenant level; if a site disables Anyone links, an Anyone default falls back to the next most restrictive value.' This states the documented reach instead of a broad caveat. The cited Set-SPOSite reference is already in sources.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: No page lists which setting removes which hero link scope.
claims.quote: `Anyone` is only available if anonymous links are allowed at the tenant level. If `Anyone` is selected but the site has Anyone links disabled, the effective default falls back to the next most restrictive value.
claims.fix: Remove ', but no page lists which setting removes which hero link scope' from the final Governance controls paragraph. The paragraph already gives the documented relationship between tenant anonymous-link policy and Anyone, and the preceding paragraph gives the site-level fallback; retain those verified statements.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph
claims.claim: The site-level audience default is the only documented administrator setting specifically for the hero link itself.
claims.quote: Searched: '"hero link" administrator controls default audience permission DefaultMainLinkScope'; read shareable-links, Set-SPOSite, Set-SPOTenant and MC1454378. Found the site audience default, no different default permission or tenant equivalent; other sharing policies are general controls.
